<!--
Read CONTRIBUTING.md before opening a PR. Solve one underlying problem.
The same requirements apply to drafts. Draft status does not defer triage or closure.
Use a conventional commit title in plain language, e.g. "feat(cli): add 'stackbase add' command" or "fix(docker): bind ports to 127.0.0.1".
-->

## Problem

<!-- Explain the problem, user friction, or gap in 1-2 sentences. Include expected behavior,
reproduction steps, or the motivation for this change. -->

## Change

<!-- Explain how this change solves the problem. If it spans packages (CLI, templates, docs),
explain why they are needed together for the same atomic unit of work. Split independent changes. -->

## Scope

<!--
- Bug fixes: Link the issue showing the bug. For a small, obvious fix, explain why no issue is needed.
- Features / New Modules: Link the approved Discussion, RFC, or maintainer request. Unsolicited, uncoordinated feature PRs will be closed.
- Core Team / Roadmap: State the milestone or initiative this satisfies.
-->

## Verification

<!-- Describe the focused tests or manual checks you ran and the observed results for the changed behavior.
"Tests pass" alone is insufficient; broad repo-wide checks are not required. State anything you could not verify.

For CLI or UI changes, include the command transcript, reproduction output, or screenshots. Upload evidence to GitHub; never commit PR-only media files. -->

<!-- If you used an agent, end with the model and harness that did the work. -->
